nodes.description: Antifibrinolytic treatment, for which the chapter's named example is tranexamic acid, used alone for some hemostatic challenges or in combination with treatment that raises von Willebrand factor.

evidence.snippet: Antifibrinolytic treatment (e.g., tranexamic acid) can be used alone for some hemostatic challenges or in combination with VWF-increasing treatment.
Useful adjunctive hemostatic treatments include antifibrinolytics, hormonal therapies for female reproductive tract bleeding, and local anatomic measures.
Other treatments that can reduce symptoms include fibrinolytic inhibitors and hormones for menorrhagia.

nodes.description: Vasopressin analog used to stimulate endothelial release of endogenous von Willebrand factor and control mild bleeding episodes.

evidence.snippet: Depending on the von Willebrand disease type, mild bleeding episodes usually respond to intravenous or subcutaneous treatment with desmopressin, a vasopressin analog.
MANAGEMENT: Targeted therapy: VWF replacement; desmopressin.
